body: Across 27 Indian winner windows, 17 began at trailing P/E ≤15 (Bajaj Finance 9, Astral 8, Eicher 13, Balkrishna ~2, APL Apollo 5, Deepak 8.5, Tata Elxsi 5, KPIT 8.5, Cochin 5.5, Mazagon 7, HAL 6, Avanti 13, Caplin 12.5, BSE 14, Garware 5, Alkyl 8, BEL 13); their median price multiple was ~266x. Three began at ≥35x (Dixon 40, Kaynes 104, Trent 155, where Trent's EPS was COVID-depressed); their median was ~19x. Two boom-time IPOs at 84x and 214x (Waaree, Premier) tripled EPS and still trade below their first close. Most low-P/E starts were not obscure: they were well-known companies in a panic (Mar 2009, Mar 2020) or companies misclassified as commodity businesses (Balkrishna, APL Apollo, Garware, Avanti). Practical rule for screening: the twin engine needs a low starting multiple. A great business bought at 100x+ has spent the multiple engine, and its return is capped at EPS growth minus de-rating. Caveat: survivorship bias. These are winners picked with hindsight, and many low-P/E stocks stayed cheap or failed (see case_study:suzlon, case_study:capital-goods-2007).
title: Starting P/E ≤15 → median ~266x; starting P/E ≥35 → median ~19x
